$comment: browserGlass CLI contract v1 (frozen in P0). Mini-language, checked by tests/py/test_contract.py: a spec has 'type' (string or list of: object, array, string, number, integer, boolean, null) or 'ref' (name in defs); object specs list 'fields' and are closed (no extra keys); a field is required unless 'required': false; other keys: enum, pattern (re.search, anchor it), min, max (number bounds; min = minimum length for strings), items (array element spec), min_items, unique, default (settings only), doc.

profile_id.doc: first 12 hex chars of sha256(os.fsencode(os.path.realpath(path))): the canonical absolute profile path, symlinks resolved; compute it only through browserglass.profile_id()

reason.doc: active when glass is on, else why it is off

tilde_path.doc: paths are always shown relative to HOME

domain.doc: an excluded host, as normalize_domain() gives it: lowercase ASCII (IDN as xn--), scheme/path/port/'*.' dropped, a leading 'www.' kept as entered (like v0); it covers that host and its subdomains

site_name.doc: my-internet style key without .css, as v0 matched it: 'x.com' and '+x.com' both cover x.com and its subdomains (a leading 'www.' is dropped; the plain name wins over '+x.com' when both exist; a more specific style, e.g. gist.x.com, wins on its own subdomain); '-x.com' covers x.<any TLD> and www.x.<any TLD>. sites.load (P2) strips surrounding whitespace from keys (upstream has 'bestbuy.com .css'; in v0 such a key could never match, documented difference) and drops a key that still fails this pattern; when a stripped key collides with an existing one, the untouched key wins

site_domain.doc: a host ('x.com'), every subdomain ('*.x.com') or every TLD ('x.*'). css-mapping.json targets that fail this pattern (upstream has '-cifraclub.com.br') are dropped: no hostname starts with '-', so v0's literal match never hit either

restart_needed.doc: files changed since this browser started

applied.doc: generated files and user.js block match the current state

companion_state.doc: the companion add-on in one profile: off (liveControl false), installed (xpi present and named in extensions.json, active), disabled (xpi present, its extensions.json entry inactive, userDisabled or appDisabled: kept in place, enabled again in about:addons), pending_restart (deposited, not loaded yet), outdated (the running add-on speaks another protocol: restart again; status only), signing_enforced (unsigned fallback only: Firefox release/esr/beta channel without a usable signed xpi in companion/, nothing deposited; with the signed xpi these channels get the deposit), signing_required (the browser deleted the xpi: no new deposit until its version changes), removed_by_user (gone from a build that never deletes it, LibreWolf or Firefox nightly/aurora/default, or after a sync saw it registered: removed in the browser, no new deposit until liveControl is turned off and on), unsupported_variant (Flatpak/Snap), no_plugin_dir (sync without --plugin-dir, or never deposited: left as it is)

first_run.doc: no v1 state existed before this sync (daemon toast)

running_changed.doc: subset of changed whose browser is running

live.doc: the exclusion list pushed to the companion add-on (none with --profile or liveControl off): hosts = browsers whose native host got it, acked = those whose add-on applied it

companion.doc: only with --plugin-dir: the companion add-on state of each synced profile

dms_opacity.doc: the DMS global window opacity read now (windowrules.kdl), whatever opacity_source says

enabled.doc: the liveControl setting of the last full sync

state.doc: off (liveControl false), connected (a native host of the current protocol runs), waiting_restart (deposited in a profile that is not disabled, no such host yet: none, or only outdated ones), disabled (deposited only in profiles where it is disabled in the browser), removed (deposited nowhere, and removed_by_user in a profile), unavailable (deposited nowhere)

hosts.doc: native host sockets whose process is alive (never connected to)

manifest.doc: our native messaging manifest is in ~/.mozilla/native-messaging-hosts

domains.doc: where the style applies: [x.com, *.x.com] for 'x.com' and '+x.com', [x.*, www.x.*] for '-x.com', then the css-mapping.json targets of that style (exact hosts, www. implied, as in v0)

opacity.doc: 0..1; the QML slider stores an int percent, logic.js divides by 100

liveControl.doc: companion add-on and native host (live exclusions)

darkPages.doc: under a dark theme, the companion add-on darkens light pages (Dark Reader) and their background canvas becomes glass

uninstall.doc: uninstall prints this line even when nothing was installed (then every list is empty and every flag false); exit 0, or 1 with the error line

removed.doc: profiles where a browserGlass file (chrome/dms-glass-*.css), @import line or user.js block (v0 or v1) was removed

restored.doc: profiles where a backup file or an original pref value (H2, H3) was put back

pending.doc: profiles whose browser is running: prefs.js is cleaned later by a detached clean-prefs (H6); subset of removed + restored

niri_changed.doc: dms-browser-glass.kdl or its include line in config.kdl was removed

state_removed.doc: $XDG_STATE_HOME/dms/browserGlass/ was removed; a pending profile only leaves its pending/<id>.json record there (with the lock file) until its cleanup is done, and that still counts as removed. False when the state is kept for a retry (a profile not fully cleaned: see warnings) or for a kept backup

xpi_removed.doc: profiles whose companion add-on (extensions/browserglass@companion.xpi) was removed

native_host_removed.doc: the native messaging manifest or the host wrapper was removed

active_site.doc: the site of the browser window niri shows (active-site, read-only, exit 0): either the four fields host, domain, source and age, or the error field alone (one of the answers below, also exit 0)

host.doc: host of the page, as normalize_domain() gives it

domain.doc: registrable domain of host (public suffix list); host itself for an IPv4 address or localhost; a leading www. is kept when the rest is a public suffix (www.gov.uk)

source.doc: companion: the add-on's live report; session: the browser's session file

age.doc: seconds since the session file was written (its session.lastUpdate), to 0.1 s; null for the companion, and for a session whose lastUpdate is missing or not a finite number

error.doc: no_browser: not a browser window, or a --window-id niri no longer lists; private: a private window; not_web: not an http(s) page; no_session: no readable session of a running profile; ambiguous: the current tab cannot be told for sure; unsupported: an IPv6 or unusable host, or a host that is itself a public suffix (github.io, co.uk: excluding it would exclude every site under it); outdated: the add-on and the helper speak different versions (restart the browser once more)

commands.doc: what each subcommand prints on stdout: a spec name above, 'report_lines' (plain text, see below) or null (no JSON document: clean-prefs prints nothing at all, exit 0; native-host, run by the browser, writes native messaging frames only, a 4-byte length then JSON, never a JSON line). Any command that fails prints the 'error' line instead and exits 1 (2 for a usage error); the error answers of active_site are part of its spec and exit 0
